findings.reason: a worker applying this branch would measure a treatment with one flipped gate as "worse" and delete the whole tool, so the yardstick needs a magnitude (or the same bootstrap interval the input branch uses) rather than a signed gap.
findings.text: s8's removal rule reads "its gate pass rate falls below its baseline's by more than the gap between the same-arm replicate's gate pass rate and the baseline's over the same sections"; that gap is 0 when the replicate matches the baseline and negative when the replicate passes more sections than the baseline, so the tolerance disappears exactly when the arm is stable and any single flipped gate removes the treatment, and when the replicate is worse than the baseline the rule can remove a treatment that is better than the replicate

findings.reason: a node queued off `implementable` is handed a coordinator's operational sequence as its deliverable and can never satisfy its own done-when inside its turn, so the plan would otherwise dispatch work that is guaranteed to stay open.
findings.text: §17 is declared `data-status="implementable"` while its Deliverable assigns the section drawing, the commit of the assignment, the dispatch of seven replays for each of ten sections at the lowest priority and at most three at a time, and the appending of each run id to the file as it is dispatched; the done-when then requires a promoted ledger row with a gate verdict for every id the file names, which completes only after seventy runs the coordinator dispatches by hand

response_events.note: The pass-rate tolerance is now the absolute gap between the same-arm replicate's gate pass rate and the baseline's, plus one section's share, so it never shrinks to zero or goes negative, and a single flipped gate never removes a treatment.
